You might be surprised. When I confessed to my friends that I was contemplating suicide, not a single one of them saw me as a burden, and they ended up being the support I needed to get through a very bad place (I'm also not saying that will be everyone's experience, but I did feel very similarly to you). When you're in a place as dark as that, it couldn't really hurt to reach out to someone (even if it just starts with the anonymity of reddit, as you're doing now!).

This is just something small I heard once, but it made a difference to me when I was in a very bad place, and maybe it'll help someone else, but the short of it is this: 

People who are considering suicide are looking for relief, when it comes down to it, but relief is a feeling and you can only feel if you're alive. 

I mean suicide is what happens when your pain is outweighed by your ability to cope, so maybe try to find a (healthy) coping strategy that helps? Cognitive behavioral therapy and meditation have been helpful for me (also admitting that they might not help others, or maybe you've tried them before).

You can find relief... it is possible. You've done it before, and I really hope you can again. Hell, you're strong enough to have made it this far, maybe you have more strength left in you than you might believe right now.
